title: Add plant rows for the four new twinned architecture rules to eng/rules-harness/plants.json
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: plants.json has plant rows for the four SL-043 twinned entries (TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags, NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core), NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App), TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore): missing
Plant outcomes for the new rows come from recorded harness runs with the TAAD engine (--engine-root), not hand-guessed: missing
Row IDs: F20-F23 continue the must-fire series, but the spike's X01-X04 names would keep the spike record traceable to the committed rows.
Where the run evidence lives: .taad/slices/SL-075/ versus a committed record next to plants.json under eng/rules-harness/. The proposal keeps eng/ free of new artefacts.
Whether the Core and App halves of NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure get one row each (chosen) or share a single row, given one xUnit Fact covers both.

RuleCases.ps1 C-008 exercises only F01-F16 ($MustFire = 1..16). F17-F23 are measured only by a plain harness --scenario plants/all run. This lap shows why that matters: a yaml change in another slice (SL-074) broke three rows, and only a full harness run caught it, not `dotnet test` or RuleCases. Deriving $MustFire from the F-rows in plants.json would put them under RuleCases.

When a slice deletes or renames a settled fitness entry, nothing flags the plants.json `also_settled` rows that name it until someone runs the harness with the engine. A cheap check that every `also_settled` name is a rule in fitness.yaml (in rules-parity or in the harness's load_rows) would catch that at edit time.
